correctness.rationale: Binomial column coefficients p_{n,j} for φ_t^n give collision mass ∑_j p²=c_t n^-1/2+O(n^-3/2). Exceptional dyadic output weights remove at most O(log n)n^-1 mass, so normalized lacunary column norm squared=c_t n^(α−1/2)+O(n^(α−1)log n). Distinct dyadic degrees have exponentially small binomial collision via exponential moment and separation m>=2n. For α<1/2 geometric column-tail Hilbert–Schmidt dominates every Schatten class; for α=1/2 Gram=c_t I+trace class and essential singular value sqrt c_t; above, column norms unbounded. Classical Hardy boundedness on nondyadic input complement completes full sufficiency. Independent binomial moment calculations n up to 4096 verify c_t convergence, not general proof.
